absent: Implementation of show_cpuinfo_core and show_cpuinfo_misc and their output fields.
Contents and ordering of capability flag name tables, bug flag table, virtualization flag table, and power flag table.
Numeric addresses and bit layouts of control, quality, sub cluster, and extended configuration registers.
Field layouts of processor identification unions and cache information structures.
Semantics of online and offline notifications, default control computation, and mount option handling for code data prioritization.
Lifecycle of pseudo lock regions and their interaction with control domain teardown beyond back pointer clearing.
Source of sub cluster node count, assignable counter global enable transitions, and per processor frequency query.
Lock ordering, sleeping context, and interrupt safety beyond the domain list mutex and read copy update discipline.
Allocation failure retry, error propagation to user space, and resource identifier exhaustion handling.
Per processor quality state structure layout and update paths.

findings.text: The lane exposes a sequential file operations table for processor information that binds start next stop and show handlers to iterate online processors and render one record each. The table is globally visible for proc registration.

Iteration starts from one before the requested position and advances to the next online processor, returning a pointer to that processor data when inside the allowed identifier range and signalling end otherwise. Advancing increments the position and reuses start logic while termination does nothing.

Per processor rendering always succeeds and ends with a blank line. Missing vendor and model names fall back to unknown wording, stepping is numeric when either stepping is nonzero or cpuid level is nonnegative and otherwise unknown wording, microcode and cache size appear only when nonzero, frequency appears only when timestamp counter feature is present with unknown wording on negative lookup and megahertz with fractional part otherwise, bogomips is derived from loop count scaled by timer frequency, and on sixty four bit builds TLB size appears only when positive followed by flush size alignment and physical and virtual address sizes.

User visible processor information uses stable labels in order for processor index vendor family model model name stepping microcode frequency cache size core and miscellaneous sections flags optional virtualization flags bugs bogomips TLB size flush size alignment address sizes and power management. Flags bugs and power entries are space separated token lists with numeric fallback for unnamed power bits.
A per task thread feature reporter emits two labeled lines for current and locked thread features by delegating token rendering to a shared helper that inspects the target task thread state.

Thread feature output uses two stable line labels for current and locked sets with token names for shadow stack and write to shadow stack capabilities, each token followed by a space and each line terminated by newline.

The lane exposes architecture helpers to look up a resource by level, compute system wide monitor identifier count, query class identifier count, apply pending control writes on a processor, refresh code data prioritization configuration, handle monitor domain online transition, and enable assignable memory bandwidth counters.
A static mutex serializes mutation of control and monitor domain lists. Add and remove paths for both kinds require the holder to own this mutex, verified by assertion checks.

Domain list membership uses read copy update semantics with tail insertion on creation and removal plus grace period wait before offline notification and memory release on teardown, allowing concurrent readers during updates.

A fixed five element hardware resource table describes cache and memory controls. Each entry pairs a generic resource descriptor with list heads for control and monitor domains plus optional scope schema format and memory or cache tuning. Two cache entries bind a capacity update writer, while memory entries use range schemas and the package performance entry is monitor only.

Discovery uses processor identification leaf 0x10 for cache and memory bandwidth with small subleaf indices and leaf 0x80000020 for AMD memory variants. Control programming targets per resource base registers indexed by class identifier, quality configuration registers for code data prioritization per cache level, an extended configuration register for assignable counters, and a sub cluster configuration register.

Resource lookup rejects levels at or beyond the table size with a null result and otherwise returns the embedded generic descriptor. System monitor identifier count is the minimum across monitor capable resources, or zero when no such resource exists, with index count equal to identifier count on this architecture.

Hardware wrappers embed generic descriptors and are recovered by container arithmetic for resources and control and monitor domains. Additional global state comprises per processor quality and monitor state, a global allocation capability flag, and a common log prefix for messages.

A legacy cache allocation probe attempts a safe write of a twenty bit all ones mask followed by a readback. Mismatch or access failure leaves capability disabled with no side effects, while full match enables allocation with four classes length twenty shared and minimum bit constraints and no sparse mask support.

Intel memory discovery derives class count from maximum cos plus one and delay range from maximum delay plus one, assumes linear mapping need, and selects per thread or maximum throttling by processor capability. AMD memory discovery selects subleaf by resource kind, derives class count from returned maximum plus one, derives maximum bandwidth as a power of two from the reported exponent, disables delay handling, uses undefined throttling, and sets minimum zero with unit granularity.

Non linear memory delay tables are unimplemented and always report failure after logging boot processor identity, causing Intel nonlinear discovery to fail. Direct delay to bandwidth conversion likewise warns once and clamps to maximum when linear mode is off.

Cache discovery derives class count and mask length from processor identification maxima plus one, masks reported shareable bits to the valid width, records sparse mask support from the non contiguous indicator on Intel only, enables input output allocation via an explicit setter, and marks the resource allocatable.

Code data prioritization is marked capable but left disabled by default with enablement expected through a mount option. Reconfiguration does nothing unless capable and otherwise programs the level specific quality register to enabled or cleared state, invoked when control domains are added or when per processor configuration is present on join.

Control programming iterates a half open class range and writes each entry to base plus index. Cache and AMD memory writers store values directly while Intel memory writers translate through a bandwidth to delay mapping. A generic update entry point dispatches through the per resource writer hook.

Control domain addition for a processor resolves the scope identifier, joins the existing domain by adding the processor to its mask when found, else allocates a node local domain, initializes identity type and mask, refreshes prioritization state, initializes and programs default controls, brings the domain online, and links it for readers. Any allocation programming or online failure discards the new domain.

Monitor addition resolves the scope identifier, joins existing domains by mask update, and otherwise creates type specific domains. Level three cache creation also refreshes assignable counter state when supported, while package performance creation uses a dedicated constructor. Top level dispatch consults allocation and monitoring capability flags to decide which path runs.

Removal clears the processor from the domain mask and retains the domain while any member remains. Last member removal validates the header, unlinks with grace wait, sends offline notification, then frees type specific state. Control removal also disconnects any pseudo lock back pointer to avoid dangling reference.

Domain identity derives from cache information for level two and level three cache scopes, from node identity for level three node scope, and from physical package identity for package scope. Any other scope yields an invalid argument error.

Invalid scope identifiers, missing domains on removal, missing cache information, failed allocations, failed control setup, failed online transitions, and unknown resource kinds are handled by one time or single warnings followed by silent return or discard, without propagating errors to callers except for internal setup allocation failure.

Level three monitor domains allocate one state array per enabled bandwidth event sized by monitor identifier count with element size of the architecture event state. Partial allocation failure releases all previously allocated arrays and fails creation, while teardown releases each index array before releasing the domain.

Monitor online clears the lowest bit of the sub cluster configuration when more than one node shares a cache, otherwise doing nothing. Assignable counter enablement toggles a dedicated bit in the extended quality register according to the stored per resource flag.

Two definitions share the package monitor constructor name where the header version is an empty no operation fallback and the source version performs full allocation and online linkage. Build selection determines which behavior applies, so callers cannot assume creation occurred.

Default control initialization fills one entry per class identifier using a shared default query and immediately programs the full range to hardware during domain setup, establishing an uncontrolled state of full cache masks and full bandwidth before linkage.
